#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored

<!-- The ledger clarity workflow: bring open gap-ledger rows to the present, as a Workflow run of a writer, a checker and a judge per chunk; how to run it and what to do with its output. -->

# The ledger clarity workflow

`ledger-clarity.js` rewrites open rows of `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` so that each states its gap as it stands now: a claim that names no fixed half, a reproducer that reproduces it, notes without a repair story. It follows the health check of 2026-10-22 (`explorations/coordinator/ledger-health-2026-10-22/REPORT.md`, sections 5.5 and 6.1), whose rubric is the record's (`explorations/reviews/revival-record-synthesis.md`). It writes nothing to the ledger.

For each chunk of about twelve rows: an Opus writer assesses each row and writes its new line, a close, or an investigate question (`writer.md`); an Opus checker verifies them against the tree (`check.md`); a judge applies or holds each, once (`judge.md`).

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger-clarity/ledger-clarity.js',
               args: { out: '/abs/folder/', chunks: [{ name: 'l1', rows: ['8', '20'] }] } })

After a chunk: for each line of `final.rewrite`, `ledger.py rewrite N FILE` (one line per file); for each line of `final.closes`, `ledger.py close`; then `ledger.py check` and `ledger.py landing-check BASE`; commit the ledger, its history and the chunk's files; file `queue.md` in `review-queue.md`. Resume a killed run with the same script path, `resumeFromRunId` and the same args.
=====
<!-- The ledger clarity workflow's checker: verify each rewritten row and each proposed close against its sources. -->

You check a writer's rewrite of open rows of the Fortress revival's gap ledger. Load the `fortress-repo` skill first (its records part). Change nothing tracked: write only `check.md` in your folder. Commit nothing.

Read your folder's `assessment.md`, `rows.rewrite` and `closes.txt`, and each row as the ledger holds it now (`python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py show N`).

For each new line:
- **Fidelity.** Every claim in it holds in the tree as it is now: open each cited `file:line`, each test, each commit. It claims no more than its evidence shows: the path (walk or the compiled path), the call form, the values, the conditions. Nothing true that the old line said, and that a worker needs, is lost without a home (a sibling row, a FACTS entry, the history).
- **Present.** It states the gap as it stands, with no story of batches, rungs or repairs.
- **Reproducer.** The named test reproduces the claim, or the cell says `none`.
- **Form.** `ledger.py check --rows` passes it.

For each close: the commit is in `HEAD`'s history and fixes what the row claims, and the test asserts it.

For each row, write in `check.md`: pass, or each failure with the passage and the source that shows it, and the correction. Run no build or test program. Your final message: the counts of pass and fail, and each failure in one line.

- F-228 **Under walk, a reduction or a comprehension that writes no static argument instantiates its big operator by a declared type, else by the join of its elements' run-time types, else at its bound, where an F-bounded parameter stays open.** It builds P-48. The declared type is a local variable's, or a top-level or local function's declared return type, for either also where the clause form ends a block. A method's return type, a top-level variable, a field, an assignment, a function expression, a branch, a call's argument and another clause form's body do not direct it. Otherwise the clauses run once into the library's collector, `__elemsOf`, which keeps the elements in order, typed at the join of their run-time types, and the operator is instantiated at that join; the reduction then runs over the collected elements, so each body runs once. A declared type or a join that does not fit falls back to the instance that no hint gives: a plain-bounded parameter takes its bound, and an F-bounded one stays open (F-143). So a `SUM` of `ZZ32` and `RR64` values, whose join `Number` is outside the bound, runs with each `+` at its operands' types. The same holds with no element and no declared type. With the big operator so instantiated, the library types `__bigOperator`'s local function `body(i: I)` at the element type `I`. A big operator whose declared result is a trait of its own is read through the `BigReduction`, `Comprehension` or `BigOperator` that the trait extends (row 718, fixed). Still wrong, each a ledger row: an empty clause form that no declared type directs takes its bound or stays open (row 716); a comprehension that no declared type reaches is built at its elements' run-time class, as `ArrayList[\Int\]`, which a declared `List[\ZZ32\]` refuses (rows 20, 717); a clause form that is a call's argument gets no declared type (rows 510, 705). Gated by `tests/UnwrittenListMapComprehensionWalk`, `UnwrittenComprehension*Walk`, `ComprehensionTypedBindingWalk`, `UnwrittenSetBigOperatorsWalk`, `UnwrittenEmptyFloatSumWalk`, `IntMapComprehensionTypedWalk` and `UserBigOperatorResultTraitWalk`. content.content:
- F-55 **Static arguments are inferred with coercion on both paths: the compiled checker from the arguments' static types and the expected type, walk from their run-time types.** So a mixed-width call takes the narrowest type into which its arguments convert, as P-74 decides. F-73 gives the checker's rule and F-137 walk's; F-87 lists where the checker has an expected type. Under walk, a typed binding converts a call's result after the call and does not fix the call's static arguments: `a: BoxK[\ZZ64\] = wrapK(3)` infers `T` from `3` as `Int` and is refused, since no coercion converts a `BoxK[\Int\]` (row 510). On the compile path, a parameter with no written bound is bounded by `Object`, not `Any` (row 412), so a parameter that nothing fixes takes `Object` there (F-78). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferCoercionShapes` and `tests/InferCoercionRungK`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 9.

- F-74 **Under walk, an integer numeral takes its type from its value: a `ZZ32` if it fits 32 bits, a `ZZ64` if it fits 64 bits, a `ZZ` above that; it stays so until walk has the checker's static types, since without them a list of numerals and a generic's static argument take their types from the values.** Its run-time type is the library's value object `Int`, `Long` or `BigNum`, below `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:125`, `:128`, `:223`). Walk instantiates a generic at it, so a `Box[\Int\]` is a type apart from `Box[\ZZ32\]` and dispatches past it (row 364). F-74 is why P-76's walk half waits; F-79 is the library half, built. Probe Q (`compile-ladder/plan-n/probe-q/PROBE-Q.md`) measured walk with every integer numeral an `IntLiteral`, the numeral's own type in the library. It ran before climb batch N's second run and before the library half landed. Alone, the switch changed 59 test verdicts. With four devices (a numeral at an `AnyIntegral` parameter read as `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, a tuple of numerals converted at dispatch, `asif` converting, a varargs list converted at dispatch), the library loaded and both microGPT checks kept their values, but 24 passing interpreter tests failed: 6 by design, 3 of them team tests that assert a `ZZ32`; 9 for want of static types (rows 364, 510); and 9 walk gaps. A size used as a value is a `ZZ32` up to 2^31-1 and a `ZZ64` above (row 486; F-140). Detail: `reviews/numeral-switch-judgement.md` sections 2 and 3.

content.content: - F-137 **Under `walk`, a generic call's static arguments are inferred with coercion, by P-74's promotion, also for the declaration that an overloaded call chooses (P-46).** A lone type parameter is one that is the whole declared type of some argument and that no other argument fixes through a type such as `List[\T\]`. It takes the narrowest of its arguments' run-time types, their coercion targets and its bounds that admits every argument. So `ZZ32` with `ZZ64` gives `ZZ64`. `ZZ64` with `RR64` gives the declared bound, the only candidate that admits both, since a `ZZ64` goes into `RR64` only when written out (P-74). With no narrowest candidate, the parameter takes its bound where every argument is below the bound (F-141), and otherwise the arguments' join. Walk promotes from the run-time types, a default. So where a static type is wider than its value, the two paths instantiate differently (row 509). The rule does not reach these open defects: a big operator over a list of numerals with no static argument (row 432); a `nat` parameter used as a value at an `NN32` binding, refused at the binding (row 486); a static argument that only the call's result mentions, at a typed binding (row 510); and a varargs or tuple parameter over mixed widths (row 511). Nor does it reach, by inference and not measured, a numeral that fits `ZZ32` passed alone for a parameter whose bound a `ZZ32` neither extends nor coerces into, since walk reads such a numeral as a `ZZ32` (P-76). Gated by `tests/InferCoercionRungK.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 9.

component p2_ascribe
import List.{...}
export Executable

object V(var data: RR64, children: List[\V\], grads: List[\RR64\])
  getter asString(): String = "V(" data ")"
  opr +(self, o: V): V = V(data + o.data, <| self, o |>, <| 1.0, 1.0 |>)
  opr -(self): V = V(-data, <| self |>, <| -1.0 |>)
end

konst(d: RR64): V = V(d, <|[\V\] |>, <|[\RR64\] |>)

sumdata(xs: List[\RR64\]): RR64 = SUM[x <- seq(xs)] x

run() = do
  a = konst(1.0); b = konst(2.0)
  c = a + b
  println("c = " c)
  println("children " |c.children| " grads " |c.grads|)
  println("sumdata unascribed literal list = " sumdata(<| 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 |>))
  (* known counter-example claim: literals stay FloatLiteral *)
  g: List[\RR64\] = <| 1.0, 1.0 |>
  println("g[0] = " g[0])
end
end

component p1_infer
import List.{...}
export Executable

object V(var data: RR64, children: List[\V\], grads: List[\RR64\])
  getter asString(): String = "V(" data ")"
end

run() = do
  a = V(1.0, <|[\V\] |>, <|[\RR64\] |>)
  b = V(2.0, <|[\V\] |>, <|[\RR64\] |>)
  (* spec basic/expressions/aggregate.tex: "The type of a list expression is
     List[\T\] where T is the union type of the types of all element expressions" *)
  l1 = <| a, b |>            (* no ascription, elements of known type V *)
  println("l1 size " |l1| " first " l1[0])
  l2 = <| a.data, b.data |>  (* RR64 elements *)
  println("l2 " l2[0])
  l3 = <| 1.0, 1.0 |>        (* float LITERALS *)
  println("l3 " l3[0])
  l4 = <| (x.data) | x <- l1 |>   (* comprehension, no ascription *)
  println("l4 " l4[0])
end
end

component tparallel
export Executable

(* Characterize implicit tuple-parallelism in the interpreter: where the
   work runs (primordial task vs forked tasks) and what it costs.
   Companion to explorations/nprobe.fss; results in microgpt-native.md. *)

burn(n: ZZ32): RR64 = do
  var acc: RR64 := 0.0
  for i <- seq(1#n) do acc := acc 0.9999999 + 0.0000001 end
  acc
end

ms(t0: ZZ64, t1: ZZ64): ZZ64 = ((t1-t0) + 500000) DIV 1000000

run() = do
  n: ZZ32 = 500000
  _ = burn(n)  (* warm-up *)

  t0 = nanoTime()
  a = burn(n)
  t1 = nanoTime()
  println("main x1           : " ms(t0,t1) " ms")

  t2 = nanoTime()
  (b, c) = (burn(n), burn(n))
  t3 = nanoTime()
  println("2-tuple           : " ms(t2,t3) " ms")

  t4 = nanoTime()
  (d, e, f, g) = (burn(n), burn(n), burn(n), burn(n))
  t5 = nanoTime()
  println("4-tuple           : " ms(t4,t5) " ms")

  t6 = nanoTime()
  h = burn(n)
  t7 = nanoTime()
  println("main x1 again     : " ms(t6,t7) " ms")

  t8 = nanoTime()
  (p, z1) = (burn(n), 0)
  t9 = nanoTime()
  println("(burn, 0) tuple   : " ms(t8,t9) " ms")

  t10 = nanoTime()
  (z2, q) = (0, burn(n))
  t11 = nanoTime()
  println("(0, burn) tuple   : " ms(t10,t11) " ms")

  println("checksum " (a+b+c+d+e+f+g+h+p+q))
end
end
